d.why: Neelie is the bat-evolved Humanimal on Counter-Earth who takes the Guardians into her house, talks with them across the language barrier, points them to the High Evolutionary's Arête Laboratories and lends them her car.
The credited name 'U.S. Marshal' is a job description; she only hands Stark the Senate subpoena in one short scene.
'Rose Hill Sheriff' is a job description, and he only questions Ellen Brandt's badge in the bar before she kills him in one short scene.

Jack Taggart is the Extremis-addicted ex-soldier who talks with Eric Savin outside the Chinese Theatre, then overdoses and explodes, injuring Happy and creating the blast that Killian passes off as a Mandarin attack.
He kills Ying Li and Shang-Chi later kills him, but his credited name 'Gang Leader' is a job description, not a name.

Anne Marie Hoag is the Damage Control director who takes the Battle of New York clean-up contract away from Toomes's crew, which is what pushes Toomes to keep the Chitauri tech and become the Vulture.
Doris Toomes, Liz's mother and Adrian's wife, only greets Peter at the door and later collects Liz from school, two short scenes that change nothing in the plot.
Foster is the Damage Control agent who taunts Toomes into punching him in Homecoming and questions Peter with Cleary after his arrest in No Way Home, with lines in both films.

Morita is Midtown's principal, who has lines in several scenes: he gives Peter detention for skipping class and the Decathlon, lectures him and gives him a second chance, and helps Doris take Liz out of school.
Randy Vale is one of Toomes's crew: he points out that they still have the Chitauri haul, helps Schultz track the lost energy core to Midtown, and is webbed up by Spider-Man at the ferry arms deal.
Peter pleads with her and saves her on the bridge, but her credited name 'MIT Assistant Vice Chancellor' is a job title, not a name.
The S.H.I.E.L.D. technician caught playing Galaga, who reports the rotor damage to Hill, is credited under a job or nickname description, not a name, and plays no real part in the plot.
'Shalla-Bal's Daughter' is a family description, not a name, and no source gives this child any lines or part in the story.

Dag is a S.A.B.E.R. agent with lines in many scenes: he suggests that Monica touch the jump point, which tangles her with Carol and Kamala, finds the Flerken eggs, and reports the station's failures to Fury during the evacuation.
Talia is a S.A.B.E.R. agent who works the jump-point anomaly with Monica and Dag, finds the Flerken eggs, and briefs Fury on the escape-pod shortage that leads to the Flerken evacuation.
Ty-Rone is Dar-Benn's Kree advisor, who helps her hunt the Quantum Bands, studies the band and warns her of its dangers, and fits it on her wrist.
Eir is the Asgardian healer with a few lines in one short scene, where she examines Jane at the Soul Forge before Odin takes over; the scene changes nothing.

Azarel is a monster hunter in Verussa's Bloodstone hunt: she chases Jack through the maze, tells Verussa that the Bloodstone threw him back (which exposes him as a monster), and is killed fighting Elsa.
Joshua Jovan is the boastful Scottish monster hunter who chats with Jack before the hunt, attacks Elsa with an axe in the maze, and is killed by Man-Thing.
Oleksander is only a credit in Kraven the Hunter (he has bodyguards), and neither the transcript nor any wiki or plot source shows him with lines or a part in the story.
She reads young Calypso's tarot and gives her the healing potion that later saves Sergei, but her credited name 'Calypso's Grandmother' is a family description, not a name.
Aliya Kimani is only a credit in Kraven the Hunter, and neither the transcript nor any wiki or plot source shows her with lines or a part in the story.
Barnum is only a credit in Kraven the Hunter, and neither the transcript nor any wiki or plot source shows him with lines or a part in the story.
Anna Kravinoff is Sergei and Dmitri's mother, whose suicide opens the story; in a flashback she tells Sergei to promise he will never be like his father, the line that shapes his break from Nikolai.
Walter Cornwall, Julia's father, only appears briefly with her at the hospital, one short scene that changes nothing.
Ann is a guest at Mary Parker's baby shower with a few party lines in one scene that changes nothing.
Loma is a guest at Mary Parker's baby shower who calls out the party games, one scene that changes nothing.
Jean is the woman Milo flirts with at the bar, with a few lines in one short scene that changes nothing.
